title: Gilgamesh and Enkidu: The First Contest
subtitle: A violent meeting ends with recognition

learningObjectives.text: How does the Pennsylvania Tablet describe their first contest?
What happens after Gilgamesh's breast is quieted?

meeting.work: An Old Babylonian Version of the Gilgamesh Epic
meeting.author: Anonymous
meeting.translator: Morris Jastrow and Albert T. Clay
meeting.locator: Pennsylvania Tablet · Column VI · part 2; Pennsylvania Tablet · Column VI · part 2, normalized characters 105-738
meeting.excerpt: They met in the plaza of the district. Enkidu blocked the gate With his foot, Not permitting Gish to enter. They seized (each other), like oxen, They fought. The threshold they demolished; The wall they impaired. Gish and Enkidu Seized (each other). Like oxen they fought. The threshold they demolished; The wall they impaired. Gish bent His foot to the ground, [149] His wrath was appeased, His breast was quieted. When his breast was quieted, Enkidu to him Spoke, to Gish: "As a unique one, thy mother bore thee. The wild cow of the stall, [150] Ninsun, Has exalted thy head above men. Kingship over men Enlil has decreed for thee.
meeting.note: Verbatim translation from the named Old Babylonian tablet witness in this edited edition. Brackets and question marks signal textual restoration or uncertainty.

narrativeBlocks.title: Enkidu blocks the gate
narrativeBlocks.body: In this Pennsylvania Tablet witness, Enkidu prevents Gilgamesh from entering. They wrestle with the force of oxen and damage the threshold and wall.

narrativeBlocks.title: The contest changes direction
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Jastrow and Clay's tablet translation; whitespace normalized): “They met in the plaza of the district. Enkidu blocked the gate With his foot, Not permitting Gish to enter. They seized (each other), like oxen, They fought. The threshold they demolished; The wall they impaired. Gish and Enkidu Seized (each other). Like oxen they fought. The threshold they demolished; The wall they impaired. Gish bent His foot to the ground, [149] His wrath was appeased, His breast was quieted. When his breast was quieted, Enkidu to him Spoke, to Gish: "As a unique one, thy mother bore thee. The wild cow of the stall, [150] Ninsun, Has exalted thy head above men. Kingship over men Enlil has decreed for thee.”

narrativeBlocks.title: The encounter eases
narrativeBlocks.body: After Gilgamesh's wrath is appeased, Enkidu speaks of Gilgamesh's mother Ninsun and the kingship Enlil decreed. This fragment presents a turn after their struggle.

narrativeBlocks.title: Keep witness and inference distinct
narrativeBlocks.body: The surviving translated lines show a fight followed by speech. Calling it a beginning of friendship is an interpretation of that sequence, not a separate line in this excerpt.

narrativeBlocks.title: Conflict becomes a relationship
narrativeBlocks.body: The scene moves from physical opposition toward recognition, but the lesson should not imply the fragment preserves every step of their relationship.
